set.body:
Journey: Open. Track: tools (Python, out of process).

Outcome
One command produces the Neurobagel JSON-LD for a release from its participants table, its annotated dictionary and its file inventory.

Acceptance
1. sanctity-publish neurobagel reads participants.tsv (and any phenotype tables named in a small configuration), the annotated dictionary and the release inventory through the HTTP API. It builds the imaging table from the inventory without downloading images, and runs a version-pinned bagel command-line tool: pheno, then bids.
2. The exact JSON-LD, its digest and a receipt (release, tool versions, inputs) are saved and reused on a retry, because bagel generates new identifiers on every run.
3. The access link in the record points to the study's page in Sanctity, or to the DOI landing page when the release has a publication record (OPEN2). No filesystem paths appear.
4. Clear outcomes for four known cases: a release with no annotated dictionary (explain how to annotate with the Neurobagel annotation tool and add the JSON through a correction); an imaging subject missing from the phenotypic table (bagel fails on this, so report the identifiers); suffixes Neurobagel does not support (list them as ignored); and an archive release with no participants table (no record is possible, and the tool says so).
5. The tool signs in with an operator-issued credential for the steward, read from the environment. It sees only what that steward may read.
6. The default service distribution has no Neurobagel dependency.

Not in scope
Approval and withdrawal control bound to target generations (NB02, parked). Outbound federation search (NB04, parked).

Start from
- The 18 November feasibility probe with bagel 0.11.7. Its findings are in docs/implementation-plan.md under External discovery through Neurobagel.
- modules/http/src/main/scala/sanctity/http/RepositoryHttp.scala lines 125 and 182: release inventory and file read.

Evidence
A tool test on the synthetic fixture with independently expected counts.
set.title: OPEN3: Neurobagel record from an accepted release (was NB01)
